दाम.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀤𑀫𑁆𑀫 (damma, “coin”), from Sanskrit द्रम्म (drammá), borrowed from Ancient Greek δραχμή (drakhmḗ). Doublet of दमड़ा (damṛā) and दिरम (diram).

भागना.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi भागना (bhāganā), based on the past participle भागा (bhāgā, “fled, running”), from Apabhramsa भग्गिअ (bhaggia), from Prakrit भग्ग (bhagga, “fled, broken”), from Sanskrit भग्न (bhagna, “broken, defeated, lost”), from the root भञ्ज् (bhañj). Cognate with …

आसानी.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian آسانی (āsānī). By surface analysis, आसान (āsān, “easy, simple”) + -ई (-ī, “-ness”). Compare Bengali আসানী (aśani).

कपड़ा.etym: Inherited from Prakrit कप्पड (kappaḍa) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-), from Sanskrit कर्पट (karpaṭa, “garment, rag”). Cognate with Marathi कपडा (kapḍā), कापड (kāpaḍ), Bengali কাপড় (kapoṛ).

senses.gloss: immediate; very close, direct, or adjacent

ख़याल.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian خیال (xayāl), from Arabic خَيَال (ḵayāl). Cognate with Bengali খেয়াল (kheẏal), Punjabi ਖਿਆਲ (khiāl).

मुसलमान.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مُسَلْمَان (musalmān), from Arabic مُسْلِم (muslim). First attested as Old Hindi मुसलमांन (musalamā̃na).

बुनियादी.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بنیادی (buniyādī). By surface analysis, बुनियाद (buniyād, “foundation, basis”) + -ई (-ī).

फ़र्क.etym: Borrowed from Arabic فَرق (“separation”). Compare Bengali ফারাক (pharak), Punjabi ਫਰਕ (pharak), Marathi फरक (pharak).

दायाँ.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit, from Sanskrit दक्षिण (dakṣiṇa, “right, southern”), contaminated with बायाँ (bāyā̃, “left”). Doublet of दाहिना (dāhinā).

उम्मीद.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian امید (um(m)ēd, um(m)īd).

डर.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀟𑀭 (ḍara), 𑀤𑀭 (dara), from Sanskrit दर (dara).

डरना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀟𑀭𑀇 (ḍaraï), from Sanskrit दरति (darati).

senses.gloss: to clear; to glow, become radiant

निखरना.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit *𑀦𑀺𑀓𑁆𑀔𑀭𑀤𑀺 (*nikkharadi), from Sanskrit *निःक्षरति (*niḥkṣarati), from निस्- (nis-) + क्षरति (kṣarati). Cognate with Punjabi ਨਿੱਖਰਨਾ (nikkharnā) / نکھرنا (nikkharnā), Gujarati નિખરવું (nikharvũ), Marathi निखरणे (nikharṇe).

मोटा.etym: Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *मोट्ट (mŏṭṭa), perhaps from a lost substrate. Cognate with Bengali মোটা (mōṭa), Punjabi ਮੋਟਾ (moṭā).

ग़लत.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian غلط (ġalat), from Arabic غَلَط (ḡalaṭ). Compare Punjabi ਗਲਤ (galat).

खुश.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian خْوَش (xwaš). Compare Bengali খোশ (khōś), Gujarati ખુશ (khuś), Punjabi ਖ਼ੁਸ਼ (xuś).

कसम.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian قَسَم (qasam), from Arabic قَسَم (qasam). Compare Bengali কসম (qôsom), Punjabi ਕ਼ਸਮ (qasam).

सरकार.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian سَرْکَار (sarkār). Compare Punjabi ਸਰਕਾਰ (sarkār) / سَرْکَار (sarkār), Gujarati સરકાર (sarkār), Marathi सरकार (sarkār), Bengali সরকার (śorkar), Nepali सरकार (sarkār).

चीज़.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian چِیز (čīz, “object, thing, stuff”). Compare Punjabi ਚੀਜ਼ (cīz) / چِیز (cīz), Gujarati ચીજ (cīj), Marathi चीज (cīj), Nepali चिज (cij), Bengali চিজ (cij).

हड्डी.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀳𑀟𑁆𑀟 (haḍḍa) (see there for more) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀇𑀓𑀸- (-ikā-) without cluster simplification, or directly borrowed from Sanskrit हड्ड (haḍḍa). By surface analysis, हड्डा (haḍḍā) + -ई (-ī). Cognate with Punjabi ਹੱਡੀ (haḍḍī).

कसरत.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian کثرت (kasrat), from Arabic كَثْرَة (kaṯra).

साँस.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀲𑀸𑀲 (sāsa), from Sanskrit श्वास (śvāsá). Doublet of श्वास (śvās).

फूलना.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀨𑀼𑀮𑁆𑀮𑀤𑀺 (phulladi), from Sanskrit फुल्लति (phullati). See फूल (phūl, “flower”) for more. Cognate with Assamese ফুলা (phula).

मर्दानगी.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مردانگی (mardānagī). By surface analysis, मर्दाना (mardānā) + -गी (-gī).

senses.gloss: partially eaten, consumed, used by someone else (of food, utensils etc.)

जूठा.etym: Inherited from Prakrit जुट्ठ (juṭṭha) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-), from Sanskrit जुष्ट (juṣṭa, “pleased”).

नार.etym: Inherited from Prakrit णारी (ṇārī), from Sanskrit नारी (nā́rī, “woman”). Cognate with Punjabi ਨਾਰ (nār, “woman”). Doublet of नारी (nārī).

फटना.etym: Regular intransitive verb from फाटना (phāṭnā), inherited from Sanskrit स्फाटयति (sphāṭayati, “it is caused to split”), from the root स्फट् (sphaṭ). Cognate with Assamese ফটা (phota), Marathi फाटणे (phāṭṇe), Punjabi ਪਾਟਣਾ (pāṭṇā).

शुद्धि.etym: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit शुद्धि (śuddhi). Doublet of सुध (sudh).

शिद्दत.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian شدت (šiddat), from Arabic شِدَّة (šidda).

पढ़ना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀧𑀠𑀇 (paḍhaï), from Sanskrit पृथ् (pṛth). Cognate with Punjabi ਪੜ੍ਹਨਾ (paṛhnā), Nepali पढ्नु (paḍhnu).

बनाना.etym: Regular causative form of बनना (bannā). Compare Marathi बनवणे (banavṇe).

घिरना.etym: Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *घिरइ (ghiraï). Cognate with Punjabi ਘਿਰਨਾ (ghirnā).

डेरा.etym: Inherited from Proto-Indo-Aryan *ḍēra. Compare Punjabi ਡੇਰਾ (ḍerā) / ڈیرَہ (ḍerah), Nepali डेरा (ḍerā), Sindhi दड़ो (daṛo) / دڙو (dṛo), ढोरो (ḍhoro) / ڈھورو, Gujarati ડેરો (ḍero), ધોરો (dhoro), Marathi डेरा (ḍerā), Assamese ডেৰা (dera).

हज़ार.etym: Compare Assamese হাজাৰ (hazar), Bengali হাজার (hajar), Gujarati હજાર (hajār), Marathi हजार (hajār), Punjabi ਹਜ਼ਾਰ (hazār), Santali ᱦᱟᱡᱟᱨ (hajar).

लंबा.etym: Inherited from Prakrit लंब (laṃba) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-) without cluster simplification—for which compare लाँबा (lāmbā) and लाँब (lāmb)—, from Sanskrit लम्ब (lamba). Cognate with Marathi लांब (lāmba).

एतबार.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian اِعْتِبَار (i'tibār), borrowed from Arabic اِعْتِبَار (iʕtibār), from اِعْتَبَرَ (iʕtabara).

अफ़सोस.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian افسوس (afsōs), from Middle Persian ʾp̄sws (afsōs). Compare Assamese আফচোচ (aphosüs), Bengali আফসোস (aphośōs), Punjabi ਅਫਸੋਸ (aphasos).

बेवा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بیوه (bēwa). Doublet of विधवा (vidhvā).

परवा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian پرواه (parwāh), an alternative form of پروا (parwā). Compare Bengali পরোয়া (porōẇa), Marathi पर्वा (parvā).

रानी.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi रांणी (rāṃṇī), from Prakrit 𑀭𑀸𑀡𑀻 (rāṇī), from Sanskrit राज्ञी (rājñī), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hrā́ȷ́niH, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃rḗǵnih₂ (“queen”). Cognate with Assamese ৰাণী (rani), Bengali রাণী (raṇī), Odia ରାଣୀ (rāṇi), Nepali रानी (rānī), Mara…

रानी.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi रांणी (rāṃṇī), from Prakrit 𑀭𑀸𑀡𑀻 (rāṇī), from Sanskrit राज्ञी (rājñī), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hrā́ȷ́niH, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃rḗǵnih₂ (“queen”). Cognate with Assamese ৰাণী (rani), Bengali রাণী (raṇī), Odia ରାଣୀ (rāṇi), Nepali रानी (rānī), Mara…

खिलना.etym: Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *खिल्लइ (khillaï). Cognate with Gujarati ખીલવું (khīlvũ).

senses.gloss: lying flat or on the face
falling flat, ineffective (as the blow of a sword)
flat, bare (terrain), uncultivated land, deserted (a village)

पट.etym: Uncertain, maybe connected with पट (paṭ, “flat surface”).
Somehow from Sanskrit पट् (paṭ, “sudden noise”), whence also पटकना (paṭaknā, “to dash against”) and पटाका (paṭākā, “firecracker”).
Uncertain, maybe connected with पट (paṭ, “flat surface”).

पुकारना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀧𑀼𑀓𑁆𑀓𑀸𑀭𑁂𑀇 (pukkārei), ultimately onomatopoeic. Cognate with Punjabi ਪੁਕਾਰਨਾ (pukārnā).

अनजान.etym: अन- (an-) + जाना (jānā), perfective adjectival of जानना (jānnā, “to know”).
अन- (an-) + जाना (jānā), perfective adjectival of जानना (jānnā, “to know”).

पागल.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀧𑀕𑁆𑀕𑀮 (paggala). Compare Assamese পগলা (pogola), Bengali পাগল (pagol), Odia ପାଗଳ (pāgaḷa), Marathi पागल (pāgal).

वारदात.etym: Borrowed from Arabic وَارِدَات (wāridāt), plural of وَارِد (wārid, “occurring”).

कदर.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian قدر (qadr), from Arabic قَدْر (qadr). Compare Bengali কদর (kodor), Punjabi ਕਦਰ (kadar).

गुनाह.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian گناه (gunāh), from Middle Persian. Compare Bengali গুনাহ (gunaho), Gujarati ગુનો (guno), Marathi गुन्हा (gunhā), Punjabi ਗੁਨਾਹ (gunāh).

अलबत्ता.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian البته (albatta), from Arabic الْبَتَّةَ (al-battata).
Borrowed from Classical Persian البته (albatta), from Arabic الْبَتَّةَ (al-battata).

चोरी.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀘𑁄𑀭𑀻 (corī), from Sanskrit चौरिका (caurikā). See चुर् (cur).

घेरना.etym: Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *घेरइ (gheraï), or equivalently a transitive form of घिरना (ghirnā).

फंदा.etym: From a conflation of Sanskrit बन्ध (bandhá) and स्पाश (spāśa, “noose”). Cognate with Punjabi ਫੰਧ (phandh) / پھندھ (phandh), Gujarati ફાંદો (phā̃do).

सभ्यता.etym: Borrowed from Sanskrit सभ्यता (sabhyatā). By surface analysis, सभ्य (sabhya, “polite, civilized”) + -ता (-tā, “state of”).

senses.gloss: a female given name, Sabhyata, from Sanskrit

सभ्यता.etym: Borrowed from Sanskrit सभ्यता (sabhyatā). By surface analysis, सभ्य (sabhya, “polite, civilized”) + -ता (-tā, “state of”).

भेदना.etym: Semi-learned borrowing from Sanskrit भेदयति (bhedayati), with influence from भेद (bhed, “distinction”).

प्रभाव.etym: Borrowed from Sanskrit प्रभाव (prabhāva). By surface analysis, प्र- (pra-) + भाव (bhāv).

उपलब्धि.etym: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit उपलब्धि (upalabdhi). By surface analysis, उप- (up-) + लब्धि (labdhi).

नैतिक.etym: Sanskritic formation from नीत (nīt) + -इक (-ik). Compare नीति (nīti, “policy, ethics”).

senses.gloss: the punishment inflicted in naraka, the torments of hell

अफसोस.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian افسوس (afsōs), from Middle Persian ʾp̄sws (afsōs). Compare Assamese আফচোচ (aphosüs), Bengali আফসোস (aphośōs), Punjabi ਅਫਸੋਸ (aphasos).

कर्म.etym: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit कर्मन् (karman). Doublet of काम (kām) and करम (karam).

senses.gloss: a measure (how much; quantity, amount, value)

मान.etym: Borrowed from Sanskrit मान (māna), from मा (mā, “measure”).

शून्य.etym: Borrowed from Sanskrit शून्य (śūnya). Doublet of सूना (sūnā), a tadbhava.
Borrowed from Sanskrit शून्य (śūnya). Doublet of सूना (sūnā), a tadbhava.

ऊँघ.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀉𑀁𑀖 (uṃgha). Deverbal form of ऊँघना (ūṅghnā), alternatively.

senses.gloss: to feel drowsy or sleepy, doze

ऊँघना.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀉𑀁𑀖𑀤𑀺 (uṃghadi), from Sanskrit *उङ्घति (*uṅghati). Cognate with Gujarati ઊંઘવું (ū̃ghavũ) and Bengali উঙ্ঘানো (uṅghanō).

सियाह.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian سیاه (siyāh). Cognate with Sanskrit श्याव (śyāva), Russian сивый (sivyj, “grey”), Lithuanian šývas (“light grey”), Old English hīew (whence English hue).

जमाल.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian جمال (jamāl), from Arabic جَمَال (jamāl).

बाल.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀯𑀸𑀮 (vāla), from Sanskrit वाल (vāla). Cognate with Assamese বাল (bal, “pubic hair”).

सहलाना.etym: Ultimately from Sanskrit शिखर (śikhará, “peak; goosebumps”). Related to सिहराना (sihrānā), सिहरना (siharnā).

अच्छा.etym: Inherited from Prakrit अच्छ (accha) without cluster simplification, from Sanskrit अच्छ (accha). Displaced Hindi आछा (āchā), from the same source. Cognate with Punjabi ਅੱਛਾ (acchā).

senses.gloss: oh! (often with stress on the final syllable)

अच्छा.etym: Inherited from Prakrit अच्छ (accha) without cluster simplification, from Sanskrit अच्छ (accha). Displaced Hindi आछा (āchā), from the same source. Cognate with Punjabi ਅੱਛਾ (acchā).

छाती.etym: Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *छात्ति (chātti), with further etymology uncertain. Cognate with Punjabi ਛਾਤੀ /چھاتی (chātī), Kumaoni छाति, Nepali छाति (chāti), Bengali ছাতি (chati), Odia ଛାତି (chāti), Gujarati છાતી (chātī).

senses.gloss: to move, scoot, shift by sliding or scraping

सरकाना.etym: Transitive form of सरकना (saraknā) with the suffix -आना (-ānā).

senses.gloss: to rise, swell, pour forth, well

उमड़ना.etym: Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *उम्मडइ (ummaḍaï). Cognate with Punjabi ਉਮਡਣਾ (umaḍṇā) / اُمَڈْݨَا (umaḍṇā).

senses.gloss: to cause to flow or float

बहाना.etym: Compare Bengali বাহানা (bahana), Gujarati બહાનું (bahānũ) and Marathi बहाणा (bahāṇā).

बीतना.etym: Verbalized from the past participle Prakrit वित्त (vitta)—whence Hindi बीता (bītā)—from Sanskrit वृत्त (vṛtta, “passed, elapsed, completed; turned”). Cognate to Punjabi ਬੀਤਣਾ (bītṇā).

इज़्ज़त.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian عِزَّت (izzat), from Arabic عِزَّة (ʕizza). Compare Assamese ইজ্জত (izzot), Bengali ইজ্জত (ijjot), Punjabi ਇੱਜ਼ਤ (izzat).

मन.etym: Inherited from Apabhramsa मण (maṇa), from Prakrit मण (maṇa), from Sanskrit मनस् (manas).

शक.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian شک (šak(k)), from Arabic شَكّ (šakk). Compare Punjabi ਸ਼ੱਕ (śakka).

इंतहा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian اِنْتِهَا (intihā), from Arabic اِنْتِهَاء (intihāʔ).

senses.gloss: sound, quiet noise (of which the source is unknown; usually of footsteps)

एकाएक.etym: Partial calque of Classical Persian یکایک (yakâ-yak), influenced by एक (ek, “one”).

गाजर.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀕𑀚𑁆𑀚𑀭 (gajjara), from Sanskrit गार्जर (gārjara). Doublet of गज़र (gazar), a borrowing from Persian.

पड़ती.etym: From पड़ना (paṛnā, “to lie idle or useless”).

senses.gloss: A field left uncultivated for a season in order to increase its fertility; fallow or uncultivated land.

पड़ती.etym: From पड़ना (paṛnā, “to lie idle or useless”).

मूली.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit *𑀫𑀽𑀮𑀺𑀕𑀸 (*mūligā), from Sanskrit मूलिका (mūlikā). Cognate with Marathi मुळा (muḷā).

सवाल.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian سَوَال (sawāl, variant form of سُؤَال (su'āl)), borrowed from Arabic سُؤَال (suʔāl).

senses.gloss: to cause to do, to make one do

कराना.etym: From करना (karnā, “to do”). Cognate with Nepali गराउनु (garāunu).

काँच.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀓𑀘𑁆𑀘 (kacca), from Sanskrit काच (kāca), from Proto-Indo-Iranian [Term?]. Compare Old Persian 𐎣𐎠𐎿𐎣 (kāsaka, “glass”).

सरापा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian سراپا,سر (sar, “head”) + پا (pâ, “foot”).

नतीजा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian نتیجه (natīja), from Arabic نَتِيجَة (natīja). Compare Bengali নতীজা (notija), Punjabi ਨਤੀਜਾ (natījā), Sindhi نتيجو (natījo).

senses.gloss: to decay, be dilapidated, waste away; to become desolate

उजड़ना.etym: From Prakrit उज्जड (ujjaḍa, “desolate, uprooted”), *उज्जडइ (ujjaḍaï, “is desolate, uprooted”), related to Sanskrit जटा (jaṭā, “root, hair”). See the Prakrit entry for more. Compare उ- (u-, “up-”) + जड़ (jaṛ, “root”).

सराबोर.etym: McGregor and Dasa both suggest a relation to बोरना (bornā, “to drench”).

अंदेशा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian اندیشه (andēša). Compare Awadhi अंदेसा (andesā), Marwari अंदेसौ (andesau).

गली.etym: Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *गली (galī, “lane”). Cognate with Punjabi ਗਲੀ (galī) / گَلی (galī), Gujarati ગલી (galī), Sindhi ڳَليِ (g̠alyi) / ॻली, Marathi गल्ली (gallī), Bengali গলি (goli).

senses.gloss: by the grace (of), by the generosity (of)

बदौलत.etym: Compound of ब- (ba-) + दौलत (daulat), both borrowed from Classical Persian.

senses.gloss: to steal (acquire at a low price); to acquire for free

लूटना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit लुट्टइ (luṭṭaï). Cognate with Marathi लुटणे (luṭṇe).

लेटना.etym: Inherited from Sanskrit लेट्यति (leṭyati, “to deceive, sleep or shine”).

आईना.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian آئینه (ā'īna). Compare Assamese আইনা (aina), Bengali আয়না (aẏna), Odia ଆଇନା (āinā).
